text.p: French electrical equipment group Schneider Thursday reported a 27 percent rise in first-half profits and forecast sharply higher earnings for 1996.
The results, however, came in at the lower end of analysts' forecasts.
First-half net income rose 26.7 percent to 503 million francs ($97.4 million) from 397 million ($76.9 million). Sales grew to 30.045 billion francs ($5.8 billion) from 29.189 billion ($5.7 billion).
"The board of directors noted that the company achieved good results in the first half despite difficult business conditions in France and Germany," it said in a statement.
"In light of recent activity trends, both in and outside France, Schneider can hope to see a very noticeable improvement in earnings for the full year."

Operating profit rose to 1.797 billion ($348 million) from 1.736 billion ($336.2 million), while pre-tax profit from continuing operations increased to 1.450 billion ($280.8 million) from 1.198 billion ($232 million).
The group said the rise in profit from continuing operations stemmed from a 15 percent increase in economic operating income, which includes exchange rate gains.
Group sales rose 3.9 percent to 21.7 billion francs ($4.2 billion) on a current structure and currency basis, or by 3.2 percent on a comparable basis of consolidation and exchange rates.
Sales fell 2.9 percent in France due to a downturn in industrial and construction spending. Europe sales rose 9.3 percent despite a slowdown in Italy and a 2 percent fall in Germany, it said.
Sales in North America rose 5.7 percent, mainly due to sustained construction activity and Mexican recovery, it said.
Sales in the rest of the world fell 2.7 percent because of fewer contracts in some countries, but this was partl offset by a strong rise in product sales in others, it said.
